newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European gas oil shortfall vanishes in November.
newsitem.headline: European gas oil shortfall vanishes in November.

text.p: Middle distillate stocks, in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 2.55 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, in November to 295.73 million barrels, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report on Tuesday.
The build wipes out the year-on-year shortfall that has persisted for most of the year. Distillate stocks were actually 770,000 barrels higher than at the end of November 1995.
Month-on-month, distillate stocks rose by most in the Netherlands where they were up 2.62 million barrels.

Crude and oil product stocks rose by 8.64 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, in November to 1.021 billion barrels. This still left them 21.67 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, lower than at the end of November 1995.
Crude oil stocks rose 6.35 million barrels, or 1.6 percent, to 405.95 million barrels, still 8.65 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, lower year-on-year.
Gasoline inventories fell 1.66 million barrels, or 1.1 percent, to 151.09 million barrels, leaving them 6.32 million barrels, or 4.0 percent, lower than at the end of November 1995.
Fuel oil stocks were 1.24 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, down at 140.79 million barrels. This left a year-on-year shortfall of 6.35 million barrels, or 4.3 percent.
Naphtha stocks rose 2.64 million barrels to 27.28 million barrels.
Crude intake was 640,000 barrels per day (bpd) higher than in October at 11.644 million bpd, leading to a utilisation rate of 92.41 percent in November.
